findings.text: follow-on: test_map_matches_the_existing_book_and_image builds its expected value from the same primitives gs.apply composes (external + operator.internal(state) then operator._exclude_shadow_residual), so both sides move together. It cannot fail on any change to gs.apply's composition of book and image - only on gs.apply literally reordering those two calls - so it is not independent coverage of the map, and the map-fidelity measure done_when (2) states (gs.apply against the existing/analytic state at a pinned rung) is asserted nowhere independently. The observed map_relative_difference 0.0 in the fragment's MAP_ROW rows is this same tautology, not a fidelity result.

follow-on: program_identity (nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:2671) changed from _batch_identity(), which carried geometry_identity, to the tree_flatten layout identity, which excludes _geometry_identity. reduced_newton caches ReducedProgram keyed on this value via _operator_program_identity and refuses reuse with a ValueError when it changes (reduced_newton.py:2464, :2803, :3113). Same-shape operators with different geometry values now share an identity where the base raised, so a cached reduced program can be reused across geometries of one shape. The kernels take the operator as a traced argument (_image's operator_value), so such reuse is plausibly intended, but no reduced_newton test was in the delta gate and this consequence of the identity change is unverified. Reachable only because this node changed the identity; scope it as a §4/§5 verification item.
